segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Today's hearing on child care since the pandemic, macroeconomic impacts of public policy measures. I want to get right to the point. Federal child care funding is on the verge of a massive funding cliff. This cliff has the potential to cause more than three million children across this country

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: to lose their care, and the impacts will ripple throughout our whole economy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: But here's the kicker. We here in Congress have the power to stop this. And that's why we're having today's hearing, and that's why I am so happy that we have our witnesses here today: Glenn Hopkins, who runs a child care

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: center; Sarah Hardy, co-founder and COO of an infant formula company; and Catherine Edwards, an economist and an expert on the labor market.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: They

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: are here to help explain what the looming child care cliff will mean for businesses, for their

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: workers, for parents and families, and for our whole economy.
Three

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: years ago, in the early weeks of the pandemic, thousands of child care centers were forced to close their doors. These closures exposed
a

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: truth that millions of American families already knew. The child care system in America is badly broken.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: For decades, millions of working families have struggled to find care for their children, and if they are fortunate enough to find good care, millions struggle

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: to pay for it so they can go to work or to school. Access to high-quality child care is essential to our

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: economy. If mamas and daddies can't get care for their babies, they can't go to work. And if millions of parents can't go to work,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: Businesses can't find the workers they need to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: operate. And if businesses cut back because they can't find workers, then national productivity and economic growth
suffer.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: These realities hit especially hard during the pandemic. When the entire childcare industry was on the verge of total collapse, Senator Tina Smith

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: and I rang the alarm bell.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: Democrats in Congress responded to this threat
by

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: providing $50 billion in federal funding to help stabilize the childcare industry. Now, this

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: funding couldn't possibly solve every problem, but it worked, and it kept the industry afloat.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: Child care providers used those funds to help pay for rent, to keep

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: children and workers safe, to raise wages, to alleviate the massive funding shortages, and much, much more.
And

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: millions of children got the care they needed.
But

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: now the child care industry is back on the brink of disaster. Most of the child care relief funding

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: expires at the end of September, that's just 10 days from now. So what will it mean for American families if we don't invest more in child care?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Analysts estimate that 70,000 child care programs will close.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: That means nearly a quarter of a million child care workers

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: could lose their jobs and over 3 million children could lose their care. Millions of parents, especially

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: moms, will be forced to leave the labor force at a time when we're already facing an incredibly tight labor market. The ripple effects will be

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: far-reaching and devastating.
We

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: cannot let this happen. We must act, and we must act quickly.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: We have champions in the Senate willing to get this done. Last month, I joined Senator Kane, Smith, and 27 of our colleagues calling for $16 billion in emergency federal funding so child care providers can keep their doors open.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: Just last week, the White House announced support for efforts to secure additional funding for child care, and I'm willing to reach across the aisle to work with any Republican who wants to help get this done. We've got one big opportunity before us this month.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: In August, the administration sent its supplemental emergency spending requests for Ukraine disaster relief and more.
The

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: Senate has now

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: started a debate on that package, and by the end of the month, we need to reach an agreement to fund the government

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: and prevent a shutdown.
This is

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: a must-pass bill. We
need to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: keep the government going so that we can continue food safety inspections

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: and vital medical research. We must protect our national security interests in Ukraine and around the world. We have to respond to the natural disasters that have devastated communities around the nation,
including

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: in Massachusetts, and we cannot leave American families behind. We need long-term investments in child care, and we must at least keep the child care industry from tumbling off a devastating cliff. Once again, I want to thank the members of this committee and I thank our witnesses for helping to make clear the importance of

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: this investment in America's families.
